extracted.intended_audience: media organisations, newsrooms, publishers, and journalists seeking to assess or certify their practices
extracted.subtask_description: Self-assessment and optional certification of a media organisation against the Journalism Trust Initiative (JTI) standard, which evaluates transparency and the professionalism of editorial processes. Designed to produce a published transparency report and optionally obtain independent certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of the media
rubrics_metrics.description: The JTI is based on decisive and objective criteria relating to the transparency of the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the organisation publishes transparent information about its structure, governance, ownership, and funding; this transparency underpins other indicators and allows audiences and stakeholders to make informed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism of editorial processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the professionalism and robustness of the processes by which journalism is produced ('the level of “making” of journalism').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on documented editorial workflows, editorial independence, checks and balances, and consistent application of editorial standards rather than judging individual items of content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of an editorial line
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence and application of an editorial line within the organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the outlet has a stated editorial line or policy and that it is actively applied in practice (consistent editorial decision-making, documented policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of correction mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of mechanisms to correct errors and handle corrections transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clear, accessible correction policies and practices (how corrections are issued, timeliness, prominence), and evidence that corrections are actually made when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of automatically generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: How the organisation manages automatically generated content (e.g., AI-generated or algorithmically produced material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policies and controls for disclosure, verification, labeling, and oversight of automatically generated content to prevent misuse and misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal and external control (oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of internal and/or external controls to ensure journalistic standards and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate governance structures (ombudsperson, editorial review boards, external advisory bodies, audits) that provide oversight and accountability for editorial decisions and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency on the identity of the owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear disclosure of who owns the media outlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require publishable, accessible information about ownership (individuals, companies, stakeholders) so audiences can assess potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of income sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of the outlet’s income sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity about revenue streams (advertising, subscriptions, public funding, donors, sponsors) and any safeguards against financial conflicts of interest influencing editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of compliance with professional guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the organisation complies with professional guarantees and standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for membership of professional bodies, adherence to codes of ethics, documented quality-control measures, and other demonstrable guarantees of journalistic professionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of a transparency report (self-assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessment carried out within a formal, identical framework for all media that leads to publishing a transparency report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations should complete the JTI self-assessment and publish the resulting transparency report so third parties can review practices; the platform jti:app is provided for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional external certification by an accredited body
rubrics_metrics.description: An external, independent audit by an accredited body can certify the conformity of the transparency report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is optional but provides independent verification; accredited auditors assess conformity with the JTI protocol and can grant a formal certification based on the transparency report and supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-focused assessment (not individual content review)
rubrics_metrics.description: JTI assesses processes and practices rather than judging individual pieces of content on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise evaluation of systemic practices (workflows, governance, transparency) rather than content moderation decisions; this distinction differentiates JTI from other trust indicator projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary, self-regulatory adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of the JTI is voluntary and functions as a self-regulatory mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations opt in to the standard and undergo self-assessment (and optionally certification); the voluntary nature is intended to incentivise improvement rather than impose regulation.
